article.story:
Real Madrid, helped by a long-range stunner from Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappé's double, came from a goal down to hammer PSV Eindhoven 5-1 and make it five wins out of five in the league phase of the Champions League.

Jose Mourinho's side trailed at the break as Ivan Perisic netted from the spot after Aurélien Tchouaméni was adjudged to have fouled Sven Mijnans in the area, but that was as good as it got for PSV.

Federico Valverde levelled matters shortly after the resumption and Jude Bellingham came off the bench to put Real ahead before Mbappé scored twice, with Vinícius Júnior completing the rout.

The comprehensive win moves Madrid up to the top of the 36-team standings, although reigning European champions Paris Saint-Germain could leapfrog them on Wednesday when they welcome Roma to the Parc des Princes.

Bellingham was among the substitutes but the England midfielder made his presence felt after being brought on at the break following Real's struggles in the first half.

They showed early intent with Vinicius firing against a post from distance after a lung-bursting run, although Kodai Sano served notice of PSV's threat when he fired wide.

The Dutch champions were then given a penalty just after the half-hour when Tchouameni was deemed to have stood on Mijnans' toes and Perisic sent Thibaut Courtois the wrong way.

Sano then headed wide as PSV ended the half on top, prompting Mourinho to turn to Bellingham plus Ibrahima Konaté and Dean Huijsen in a triple half-time change -- and Real drew level within five minutes of the restart.

Arda Guler's clever backheel following Vinicius' cross fell straight into the path of Valverde, who buried a first-time finish beyond PSV goalkeeper Matej Kovár.

Even better was to follow on the hour mark as Bellingham collected a loose ball from around 25 yards out, chipped it up in the air then let fly with the outside of his right boot - an outstanding dipping volley that left Kovar with no chance.

Mbappé was in on the action in the 64th minute as Sano carelessly gave away the ball, allowing Guler to drive into the box before squaring for the France striker to score for the seventh Champions League match in a row.

Mbappé had his second four minutes from time when he latched onto substitute Brahim Diaz's pass, rounded Kovar and slotted into an empty net, before Bellingham teed up Vinicius for Real's fifth late on.

PA and The Associated Press contributed information to this report.
